title: Integrating the NHQ REST API: Authentication, Pagination and Webhooks
description: A practical, end-to-end guide to authenticating against the NHQ platform API, paginating large result sets and reacting to events with webhooks.
content:
Our REST API is the backbone of every NHQ integration. This guide walks through the three things every integration needs: **authentication**, **pagination** and **webhooks**.

## Authentication

All requests are authenticated with a bearer token. Tokens are issued per environment and never expire silently — you get a `token.expiring` webhook 7 days before rotation.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $NHQ_API_TOKEN" \
  https://api.nhq.example.com/v1/cases
```

> **Never** commit tokens to source control. Use your platform's secret manager and rotate quarterly.

### Token scopes

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `cases:read` | List and read support cases |
| `cases:write` | Create and update cases |
| `webhooks:manage` | Register and remove webhook endpoints |

## Pagination

List endpoints return at most 100 items. Use cursor pagination — it is stable under concurrent writes, unlike page numbers.

```ts
async function listAllCases(token: string) {
  const items = []
  let cursor: string | undefined
  do {
    const url = new URL('https://api.nhq.example.com/v1/cases')
    if (cursor) url.searchParams.set('cursor', cursor)
    const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } })
    const page = await res.json()
    items.push(...page.items)
    cursor = page.next_cursor
  } while (cursor)
  return items
}
```

## Webhooks

Register an HTTPS endpoint and we will POST signed JSON events to it.

1. Register the endpoint with `POST /v1/webhooks`
2. Verify the `X-NHQ-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256)
3. Respond `2xx` within 10 seconds — otherwise we retry with exponential backoff

Go-live checklist:

- [x] Store the signing secret outside source control
- [x] Verify signatures before parsing the body
- [ ] Handle duplicate deliveries idempotently
- [ ] Alert on sustained delivery failures

---

Questions? Open a support case with the tag `api-integration` and the platform team will pick it up within one business day.

title: Troubleshooting Data Sync Failures in the Analytics Pipeline
description: How to diagnose the four most common causes of nightly sync failures — schema drift, credential expiry, quota exhaustion and network partitions.
content:
When the nightly analytics sync fails, the dashboard shows *stale data* and clients notice within hours. This runbook covers the four most common root causes, in the order you should check them.

## 1. Schema drift

The most frequent culprit. A source system added or renamed a column and the sync job rejects the batch.

```sql
-- Compare live schema against the registered contract
SELECT column_name, data_type
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'orders'
ORDER BY ordinal_position;
```

If the schema changed, update the contract file and re-run the job with `--allow-additive`.

## 2. Credential expiry

Check the connector logs for `401` or `invalid_grant`:

```bash
grep -E "401|invalid_grant" /var/log/nhq/sync-*.log | tail -20
```

Service-account keys rotate every 90 days. The fix is a one-liner:

```bash
nhq-cli connections refresh --id analytics-prod
```

## 3. Quota exhaustion

> Warehouse quotas are shared across all clients on the same tier. A single runaway backfill can starve the nightly window.

Symptoms and remedies:

| Symptom | Likely cause | Remedy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job queued > 30 min | Slot contention | Reschedule backfills off-peak |
| `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | Daily byte quota hit | Request a temporary quota raise |
| Partial tables | Killed mid-write | Re-run with `--from-checkpoint` |

## 4. Network partitions

Rare, but the hardest to spot: the job *hangs* instead of failing. Set an explicit timeout and let the scheduler retry:

```yaml
sync:
  timeout_minutes: 45
  retries: 2
  retry_backoff: exponential
```

---

Escalate to the **Data & Analytics** team if none of the above resolves the failure — include the job id and the last 100 log lines in the case.

title: CRM Rollout Playbook: From Sandbox to Go-Live in Four Weeks
description: The standard four-week rollout plan we use for every CRM implementation — milestones, owner matrix and the go-live gate checklist.
content:
Every successful CRM rollout we have delivered follows the same four-week shape. This playbook makes that shape explicit so nothing depends on tribal knowledge.

## Week-by-week plan

### Week 1 — Sandbox and data audit

- Provision the client sandbox
- Run the data quality audit (`nhq-cli crm audit --sandbox`)
- Agree the field mapping with the client's ops lead

### Week 2 — Migration dry run

Run the full migration against the sandbox and measure:

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Record match rate | ≥ 99.5% |
| Dedup collisions | < 0.1% |
| Dry-run duration | < 4 hours |

### Week 3 — UAT and training

> UAT is not a demo. The client's own team must complete their daily workflows in the sandbox without our help before we schedule go-live.

### Week 4 — Go-live

Go-live happens on a **Tuesday morning** — never a Friday. The gate checklist:

- [ ] Dry-run migration signed off
- [ ] UAT sign-off from the client sponsor
- [ ] Rollback plan rehearsed
- [ ] Support rota staffed for the first 72 hours

## Roles

| Role | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| Account Manager | Client communication, sign-offs |
| Team Lead | Migration execution, gate decision |
| Support Engineer | Post-go-live triage |

---

*Template project plans live in the shared drive under `playbooks/crm-rollout/`. Copy, don't edit in place.*
